summary: A refactor: every CAD problem is now one kind of issue. The document check, a rebuild's feature failures and stops, its body warnings, a sketch's solver problems, refused edits and shrink warnings, Section for CAM and Send to CAM refusals, and refused section, sketch and reference curve DXF exports each map through one adapter into an issue: a stable code, a severity, a failed or blocked state, a subject named by id (the document, a feature, one of its input slots, a body key, a sketch relation, edge or point, a CAM operation and its source, or a DXF export and its source), typed details, cause links and repairs prepared at the document version. A feature that reads a failed result is blocked, and its issue names that failure as its cause. Development and tests check each issue list as a causal graph; production names any cause it cannot resolve rather than dropping it. The CAD header lists the issues of the shown build with their subject, cause and repairs. Edit feature opens the feature; Choose edges again or Choose opening again opens a Fillet, Chamfer or Shell at that choice; and the sketch header offers Delete relation for a relation the solver names as redundant or conflicting. A repair is refused once the part has changed since it was prepared. The history marks a blocked feature apart from a failed one. Agent replies to cad_get_context and cad_build carry a bounded issue digest; a refused edit, CAM step or DXF export names its feature, input slot, operation or export in error.details.issue, and a refused sketch edit also gives the issues its sketch header shows. Kernel failures now name their step and its likely cause, or say the kernel named none, and the repair. A CAD kernel or sketch solver that cannot load, start or run, or whose reply cannot be read, gives kernel-unavailable or sketch-failed with a message naming that cause and the next step. The kernel's, the solver's or the browser's own words, or the internal check that failed, are kept as kernelMessage: behind a closed Kernel message disclosure on the issue rows of the CAD header, on a sketch refusal in the sketch header and in the Section for CAM, Export DXF and import dialogs, and in agent replies, bounded to 1,024 bytes; status notices do not show them. A sketch DXF export's refusals name DXF export rather than CAM. Every other code, message and subject is unchanged across the parity corpus and main's test cases. Issue work stays linear in the length of the history and in the number of failures: the history and the header index feature names and issue keys once per list, failures index features once, and a build with no failure walks no history for blocked features. The interim sketch issue adapter that 0.0.796 added for this change is removed.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. CAD diagnostics do not reach post-facing output: issues live in the workbench and in agent replies, Section for CAM and DXF export refusals stay in their dialogs, and no package, revision, UPID or post input carries them. Agent replies change only by additions (issues, error.details.issue, error.details.issues on a refused sketch edit, details and facts on each build diagnostic, cause and kernelMessage on a sketch analysis, and the kernel's or solver's own words as kernelMessage) and by the reworded messages listed under events. Every code keeps its meaning. A kernel request that fails without a code, which an agent reply gave as OPERATION_FAILED with "Operation failed. Review the page or retry with corrected inputs." and the workbench as the kernel's raw text, now has the code kernel-operation-failed and a message naming the request, with the raw text as kernelMessage. A kernel that cannot load gives kernel-unavailable, and now so does a kernel worker that cannot start, cannot be handed a request, fails with an unexpected error or replies unreadably. A sketch solver that cannot load, start or run, replies unreadably or with its own error, or runs past its time limit gives sketch-failed with the cause solver-unavailable. Each of these was a plain error, which agents got as OPERATION_FAILED. A native sketch solver that traps, returns an invalid result, cannot be loaded or speaks another protocol, which main gave as sketch-failed judging the drawing, now adds that cause and its words, and a drawing keeps its inferred relations. A code the app does not list would arrive as kernel-unrecognised with the original in its facts, and a guard test keeps every code the kernel and the document check raise listed. Nothing on main, its end-to-end specs or its guides matched the old plain kernel or solver text, the sketch DXF texts that named CAM, or OPERATION_FAILED for CAD.

checklist.schema: No CAD document, sketch, UPID, post, machine package, saved revision, storage or journal schema change. The issue model (src/domain/cad/cadIssues.ts, cadIssueCodes.ts) is derived on each build, edit refusal, sketch analysis, refused CAM step or refused DXF export and never stored. Its namespaces are feature, kernel, body, sketch, cam and export. export is new in this change: it holds the refusals of a section, sketch or reference curve DXF export, about the subject {kind: export-operation, format: dxf-section, dxf-sketch or dxf-curve, sourceId}, with the codes each export reaches (CAD_EXPORT_STEP_CODES, pinned exactly by the diagnostics walk of each export). It is its own namespace because each namespace types its codes against the subjects they can be about: a cam issue is a CAM step's refusal about a CAM operation, and a DXF export is no CAM step; a feature issue is about the document, a feature or an input slot, and seven of the section export's codes (empty-section, degenerate-section, open-section, tangent-section, invalid-section, section-failed, unsupported-section-curve) are no feature's. CadDiagnostic gains optional details (the kernel step, the input it was reading and the kernel's own text) and facts (for selection-empty, selection-count-mismatch and kernel-unrecognised). CadError gains facts for those codes and kernelMessage. CadSketchSolverFailure is a CadError with code sketch-failed and the solver's or the browser's words as kernelMessage; native names how the native solver failed (load-failed, incompatible or failed), which the solver worker's error reply carries as failure. Sketch feedback, the sketch issue input and the cad_inspect_sketch_constraints analysis gain cause (solver-unavailable) and kernelMessage. CadBodyIssue gains reason (untracked-body-parts) and omitted (more-body-issues). All are additions; existing fields keep their meaning.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation or input-version change. Repairs check the document version they were prepared at: a stale repair is refused with stale-repair, before it changes anything. Agent tools: cad_get_context and cad_build add issues ({ items ≤ 10 within 4,096 bytes, omitted, blocked summaries within 2,048 bytes, omittedBlocked, and unresolved only when a cause resolves to nothing }). Their diagnostics keep main's bound of 10 within 4,096 bytes, now including their details. Kernel words are bounded to 1,024 serialized bytes, with an ellipsis where cut, in every reply, so a listed failure always keeps an account of them; a listed issue whose diagnostic is in the same reply names that diagnostic's position as diagnostic instead of repeating them. A refusal of cad_edit_document or a CAM step that concerns a feature, input slot or CAM operation adds error.details.issue, and so does a refusal of cad_export_section_dxf, cad_export_dxf or cad_export_curve_dxf, about the export and its source. cad_inspect_section cuts a Section for CAM step, so its refusals are the CAM issues the Section for CAM dialog shows for the same refusal. A refused sketch edit adds the refusal as error.details.issue and error.details.issues, a bounded digest of the refusal, the attempted subjects it names and the shrink warnings of the current version: the issues its sketch header shows. Its feedback and analysis stay as they were, and only a relation the accepted sketch has offers Delete relation. cad_inspect_sketch_constraints adds cause (solver-unavailable) and kernelMessage to an analysis the solver could not make. A refusal that came back from the kernel or the solver carries its own words in error.details.issue.details.kernelMessage, or in error.details.kernelMessage when no issue covers it (a kernel that cannot load, start or run). Each build diagnostic adds details and, for selection codes, facts. Tool names, descriptions and input schemas are unchanged: initial discovery is 51,178 of its 51,200 UTF-8 bytes on main and on this branch, and stays at S7's 51,154 once S7 merges first. Reply growth, measured as cad_build and cad_get_context build the reply: one failed move in three features adds 1,088 bytes (472 → 1,560: the diagnostic's details and two issues). One failed move blocking a chain of 399 adds 1,225 bytes, since blocked features are summarized by cause with the first eight ids. 300 failed pads in 400 features add 4,971 bytes (2,142 → 7,113), the items capped at 10 within 4,096 bytes (8 listed, 292 omitted). The issues add at most 4,096 + 2,048 + 256 bytes, and the diagnostics stay within main's 4,096. Message, code, severity and subject changes against main, each with its reason. Every code keeps its meaning. Each reworded message names its likely cause, or says the kernel named none, and the next step; where main's text was the only record of which internal check failed, that text moves to details.kernelMessage. The kernel's, the sketch solver's or the browser's own text is never the message and never dropped: it is kept in details.kernelMessage (at most 2,048 characters, cut with an ellipsis). The workbench shows it behind a closed Kernel message disclosure on the issue rows of the CAD header, on a sketch refusal in the sketch header, and in the Section for CAM, Export DXF and import dialogs; status notices do not show it. Agents get it, bounded to 1,024 serialized bytes with an ellipsis where cut, in diagnostics[].details.kernelMessage, error.details.issue.details.kernelMessage, or error.details.kernelMessage for a refusal no issue covers; a listed issue whose diagnostic is in the same reply names that diagnostic instead. Parity against main 735c68b6: in the 86-document corpus, 27 of the 72 build diagnostics differ (17 fillet and 5 chamfer kernel failures that now have their step message, and 5 invalid-solid), all rewordings listed here; checks, edit results, sketch issue lists, sections, topology reads and exports are identical. Main's tests, run on this branch's source with two mechanical migrations (the two test files of the interim sketch adapter renamed to the new adapter, and two files' imports of the removed cadSketchSolverMessages pointed at cadSketchSolverFailure, which keeps its constants): of the 1,591 test cases that record a refusal, build or sketch list on main, 1,542 record the same on this branch, 1 records the same once generated ids are named, 37 differ only by the rewordings listed here, and 11 differ otherwise. A rewording is judged where its message sits: records are paired by their shape (codes, features and their kinds, bodies, sketch rows and their order), each message is compared with the one at the same position, and a changed message counts as a rewording only when an explicit old → new pair for that position's code allows it, a pair whose new text and citation are written here; every new message must also be listed here. A kernel step's message is judged at its step as well: this branch records, with each build diagnostic, the step its rebuild was taking, which main's failures did not name, and a pair for one step allows a change only where that step was recorded and for a feature whose kind takes it, both by the steps read from the rebuild's source and by a list written from what each feature does, which must agree. Two messages that swap places, a step's message at another step (a fillet's failure given the chamfer's message), a listed rewording at another code, or main's own text standing in for the kernel's words therefore differ otherwise. The 37 hold 54 changes, allowed by 14 of 24 pairs; 21 are step messages, each at the step this branch recorded, and each of the 250 build diagnostics this branch recorded names a step its feature's kind takes. Of the 11, 7 kernel tests stop earlier, at main's assertion of the kernel's raw text, after a first build that differs only by its listed step message; 2 also record the sketch issues a refused agent sketch edit now builds, which their assertions allow; and 1 records a coded sketch-failed where main raised a plain error; and 1, main's test of recovery wording, feeds the feedback a rejected solve worded like a solver that could not load, which this branch, deciding by cause rather than by words, reports as the judgement it is. No case recorded on main is absent. 11 cases record only on this branch: coded kernel-unavailable (4) and sketch-failed (7) refusals where main raised plain errors or, for 5 native solver failures, returned a rejected solve. Coverage gap: what main's 7 stopped kernel tests record after that assertion (an export refusal, a later build) is not compared, and this branch's versions of those tests assert it; a message no test makes, such as the three display topology-mapping sites, is checked by reading only. Every message production code makes in any recorded test, main's or this branch's (1,671 distinct, 61 not on main's records), is on main's records, listed here, written verbatim by main's source, or written by one of main's template literals at a line this branch did not change (5); the 5 the kernel client rebuilt from a worker's coded error reply, counted apart, came from tests' stand-in workers. Codes, severities and subjects: Worker request that fails without a code (build, export, section, topology reads, imports): main "Plain error carrying the kernel's raw text. The UI showed that text; agents got OPERATION_FAILED with "Operation failed. Review the page or retry with corrected inputs."" → "kernel-operation-failed, with the request's message (below) and the raw text in kernelMessage. An error reply from the kernel worker that carries no code is one of these, whatever text it holds: a worker's uncoded text is never the message" (Raw kernel text was passed through bare, and agents could not tell a kernel failure from any other). Kernel that cannot load: main "A plain error with the browser's or the loader's text, which was kept, so every later request failed the same way until the page was reloaded" → "kernel-unavailable, with the browser's words as kernelMessage: "The CAD kernel could not be loaded; the app may have been updated, or the network dropped. Reload the page." when the kernel client's module cannot be loaded, for the shared client, feature previews and feature inputs alike; "The CAD kernel could not be loaded. Reload the page; if this repeats, use a browser that runs WebAssembly." when the kernel's WebAssembly cannot be initialized" (Names the cause, which every request shares, and the next step. A failed load is never kept: every request waiting on it fails with it, and the next request loads again. A worker whose kernel could not be initialized is retired, so a queued request and the next one start a fresh worker; other refusals keep the worker running). Kernel worker that cannot start, cannot be handed a request, fails or replies unreadably: main "Plain errors: "Unable to start the CAD worker." or the browser's words; "The CAD worker stopped. Retry the operation to restart it."; "The CAD worker response could not be read."; "Invalid CAD worker response."" → "kernel-unavailable, with the browser's words or the check the reply failed as kernelMessage: "The browser could not start the CAD kernel. Reload the page; if this repeats, use another browser or turn off extensions that block this site's scripts."; "The request could not be handed to the CAD kernel, so the kernel was stopped. Retry the operation to restart it; if this repeats, reload the page."; "The CAD kernel failed with an unexpected error and was stopped. Retry the operation to restart it; if this repeats, reload the page."; "The CAD kernel's reply could not be read, so the kernel was stopped. Retry the operation to restart it; if this repeats, reload the page."" (A failed worker fails every request it held, as a kernel that cannot load does; agents could not tell it from any other failure, and the browser's own words, such as a Content Security Policy denial, were the message. The worker is still stopped and the next request starts a new one; cancellation, disposal and a full queue keep their own errors). Sketch solver that cannot load, start or run: main "Plain errors: the browser's words when the solver module cannot load; "Unable to start the sketch solver worker." or the browser's words; "The sketch solver worker stopped. Retry to restart it."; "The sketch solver worker response could not be read."; "Invalid sketch worker response."; the worker's own error text; "Sketch solving exceeded its time limit. Retry with a smaller sketch."" → "sketch-failed, with the cause solver-unavailable and the browser's or the worker's words as kernelMessage: "The sketch solver could not be loaded; the app may have been updated, or the network dropped. Reload the page."; "The browser could not start the sketch solver. Reload the page; if this repeats, use another browser or turn off extensions that block this site's scripts."; "The sketch could not be handed to the sketch solver, so the solver was stopped. Retry to restart it; if this repeats, reload the page."; "The sketch solver failed with an unexpected error and was stopped. Retry to restart it; if this repeats, reload the page."; "The sketch solver's reply could not be read, so the solver was stopped. Retry to restart it; if this repeats, reload the page."; "The sketch solver failed on this sketch, for a reason it did not name, and was stopped. Retry to restart it; if this repeats, reload the page."; the time limit keeps main's text. A refused edit gives the message after the sketch's name and a colon" (The workbench showed a plain error and agents got OPERATION_FAILED. The sketch header now shows one issue with the words under Kernel message, in workbench edits, previews, sketch-mode commits, cad_edit_document and cad_inspect_sketch_constraints alike; a drawing keeps its inferred relations rather than retrying without them, and a module that failed to load is loaded again by the next request. Cancellation, disposal and a full queue keep their own errors). Native sketch solver that cannot be loaded, speaks another protocol, traps or returns an invalid result: main "sketch-failed, judged as a drawing the solver could not solve: a refused edit read "{sketch}: The sketch solver could not be loaded. Edit the sketch again to retry, or reload the page.", "{sketch}: The sketch solver does not match this version of the app. Reload the page." or, for a trap or an invalid result, "{sketch}: The sketch solver could not solve this edit."; a drawing was retried without its inferred relations; solves within a second of a failed load failed without trying, and a module of another protocol was never loaded again" → "sketch-failed with the cause solver-unavailable, and the browser's, the module's or the trap's words as kernelMessage. The first two keep main's text. A trap or an invalid result, also on a fresh instance after a used one failed, gives "The sketch solver failed on this sketch and was stopped. Edit the sketch again to restart it; if this repeats, reload the page.", in a refused edit "{sketch}: The sketch solver failed on this sketch and was stopped. Edit the sketch again to restart it; if this repeats, reload the page."" (A failure of the solver is no judgement of the drawing: the drawing keeps its inferred relations, and workbench edits, previews, sketch-mode commits, cad_edit_document, cad_inspect_sketch_constraints and the sketch header give the one issue. The worker names how the native solver failed, and the client words it and keeps the worker. A failed load is never kept: a solve within a second of one tries once without waiting, and a module of another protocol is tried again by the next solve). Section, sketch and reference curve DXF export refusals: main "The refusal's code and message, with no subject" → "Issues of the new export namespace about {kind: export-operation, format: dxf-section, dxf-sketch or dxf-curve, sourceId}, each keeping its own code (CAD_EXPORT_STEP_CODES, such as empty-section, missing-body, kernel-operation-failed, missing-sketch, suppressed-sketch, empty-sketch, dxf-geometry, missing-curve, suppressed-curve or dxf-arc-precision). Agents get error.details.issue; the Export DXF dialog shows the code, with the kernel's words under Kernel message, and gives a source it cannot resolve, including a section offset, the code its export would refuse it with" (An export is neither a CAM step nor a feature, and each namespace is tied to its own subject kind; the dialog and agents can now name the export and its source. A source with nothing to write stays a hint with no code). Build diagnostic with a code the app does not list: main "Passed through with that code" → "kernel-unrecognised, keeping the original code in facts.refusalCode and its message" (Consumers can rely on the code list. A guard test holds every code the kernel and the document check raise to the list, so no current code is affected). New codes: main "none" → "input-blocked (issue: "Not evaluated, because an input it reads did not rebuild."), stale-repair (refusal of a repair prepared for an earlier version: "The repair "{repair}" was prepared for an earlier version of the part. Read the issues again and choose a current repair.")" (New behaviour). Severity, state and subject: main "Diagnostics and refusals had neither" → "Issues add severity, state and subject. Refusals add error.details.issue. Diagnostic and refusal fields are unchanged" (Additions only). Kernel failures in the kernel's own words (kernel-operation-failed, one message per step). Main gave the raw kernel text when there was any, for example "Interrupted linear pattern", and otherwise "OpenCascade could not construct this feature. Reduce its dimensions or revise the sketch." Neither named the step, the cause or the next step. The raw text is now details.kernelMessage, and details names the step and the input it was reading. import: "The imported solid could not be rebuilt. The file may hold damaged or open geometry; export it again from the program that made it." profile: "The sketch profile could not be turned into a face. A contour may cross itself or be too small; edit the sketch." extrude: "The extrusion could not be built from its sketch. A contour may cross itself or the distance may be too small; edit the sketch or the distance." revolve: "The revolution could not be built from its sketch. The profile may cross or touch the axis; keep it on one side of the axis or change the angle." loft: "The loft could not connect its sections. The sections may twist against each other or differ too much; revise their shapes or try ruled mode." sweep: "The sweep could not follow its curve. The section may be too large for a bend in the curve; reduce the section or ease the bend." pocket: "The pocket could not be cut. Its profile may miss the body or cross itself; edit the sketch or choose another target." join: "The bodies could not be joined. They may touch only along a face or an edge; overlap them or move them apart." cut: "The cut could not be made. The tool may touch the body only along a face or an edge; overlap it with the body or move it away." intersect: "The intersection could not be made. The bodies may not share material; move them so they overlap." fillet: "The fillet could not be applied. The radius may be too large for an edge or a face next to it; reduce the radius or choose other edges." chamfer: "The chamfer could not be applied. The distance may be too large for an edge or a face next to it; reduce the distance or choose other edges." shell: "The shell could not be made. The thickness may be too large for a thin or curved region; reduce the thickness or choose another opening." transform: "The body could not be moved. A move copies its source body exactly, so the source body is likely damaged; rebuild the part, and if this repeats, revise the feature that made the source body." mirror: "The body could not be mirrored. A mirror copies its source body exactly, so the source body is likely damaged; rebuild the part, and if this repeats, revise the feature that made the source body." pattern: "The pattern could not be built. Copies may touch each other only along a face or an edge; change the spacing or the count." check: "The result is not a valid closed solid. A dimension may make faces meet or vanish; revise the inputs of this feature." record: "The result could not be prepared for display and selection. A dimension may make a face too small to draw; revise the dimensions of this feature slightly." Worker requests that fail without a code (kernel-operation-failed; main gave the raw text). Outside every feature step nothing names a cause, so the message says the kernel named none; reading a file names the file as the likely cause: build: "The part could not be rebuilt, for a reason the kernel did not name. Rebuild again; if this repeats, undo the last change." export: "The part could not be written to the file, for a reason the kernel did not name. Rebuild the part and export again." section: "The section could not be cut through this body, for a reason the kernel did not name. Move the section plane slightly or choose another body." topology reads (inspect, resolve picks, adjacency, tangent chain): "The faces and edges of this body could not be read, for a reason the kernel did not name. Rebuild the part and select again." solid import: "The file could not be read as a solid. It may be damaged or hold no closed solid; export it again from the program that made it." DXF import (sketch and curve): "The DXF file could not be read. It may be damaged; save it again as DXF and retry." any other: "The CAD kernel could not complete this operation, for a reason it did not name. Retry the operation; if this repeats, reload the page." Reworded refusals, same code: invalid-solid: main "OpenCascade rejected the resulting topology. Reduce the dimensions or choose a different feature." → "The result is not a valid closed solid: some of its faces cross or leave gaps. Reduce the dimensions of this feature or revise its inputs." (Named the kernel, not the cause). extrude-invalid, revolve-invalid: main "OpenCascade rejected the {operation} topology. Revise the profile or direction." → "The {operation} left a body whose faces cross or leave gaps. Revise the profile or the direction." (Named the kernel, not the cause). empty-solid: main "The profile did not produce a native solid." → "The sketch profile made no closed solid. A contour may be open or too small; close or enlarge it in the sketch." (No cause or next step). shell-failed (outward): main "The kernel shell extended outside the original body instead of producing inward walls." → "The shell grew outside the body instead of making inward walls. Reduce the thickness or choose another opening." (No next step). shell-failed (builder): main "OpenCascade could not shell this body. Reduce the thickness or choose another planar opening." → "The shell could not be made. The thickness may be too large for a thin or curved region; reduce the thickness or choose another planar opening." (Named the kernel, not the cause). selection-tangent-chain: main "OpenCascade would {fillet or chamfer} additional tangent edges. Enable Follow tangent edges or select the complete tangent chain explicitly." → "The {fillet or chamfer} would also reach edges tangent to the selected ones. Enable Follow tangent edges or select the complete tangent chain." (Named the kernel, not the feature). kernel-operation-failed (edge builder): main "OpenCascade could not {fillet or chamfer} the selected edges. Reduce the radius or revise the selection." → "The {fillet or chamfer} could not be applied to the selected edges. The {radius or distance} may be too large for an edge or a face next to it; reduce the {radius or distance} or choose other edges." (No cause. A chamfer now names its distance, not a radius). kernel-operation-failed (tangent chain): main "The native tangent chain left this body. Rebuild and select again." → "The tangent edges found from this edge left the body. Rebuild the part and select again." (Internal wording). pocket-tool: main "OpenCascade could not extrude the through-all cutting face." → "The pocket could not make its through-all cutting tool from the sketch. A contour may cross itself; edit the sketch." (No cause or next step). loft-invalid (validity): main "OpenCascade rejected the loft topology. Revise the section shapes or try ruled mode." → "The loft made a body whose faces cross or leave gaps. Revise the section shapes or try ruled mode." (Named the kernel, not the cause). loft-invalid (no solid): main "The loft did not produce a native solid." → "The loft made no closed solid. The sections may cross each other or one may be open; revise the sections or try ruled mode." (No cause or next step). loft-failed: main "OpenCascade could not connect these sections. Revise their shapes or try ruled mode." → "The loft could not connect these sections. They may twist against each other or differ too much; revise their shapes or try ruled mode." (Named the kernel, not the cause). loft-placement (two): main "OpenCascade could not place the fitted loft in its datum frame. / Datum placement did not preserve the native loft solid." → "The loft could not be moved onto its datum plane. The move copies the loft exactly, so the loft built before it is likely damaged; rebuild the part, and if this repeats, revise its sections or recreate the datum plane. Main's sentence moves to kernelMessage." (No cause or next step). sweep-invalid (validity): main "OpenCascade rejected the exact Sweep topology. Revise the section or curve." → "The sweep made a body whose faces cross or leave gaps. Reduce the section or ease the bends of the curve." (Named the kernel, not the cause). sweep-invalid (segment): main "Sweep segment did not produce a native solid." → "The sweep made no closed solid along curve segment {n}. The section may be too large for that segment; reduce the section or revise the segment." (No cause; now names the segment). sweep-failed: main "OpenCascade could not construct curve segment {n}." → "The sweep could not follow curve segment {n}. The section may be too large for that segment; reduce the section or revise the segment." (Named the kernel, not the cause; keeps the segment). section-failed: main "OpenCascade could not compute an exact planar section." → "The section could not be cut through this body. The plane may run along a face or an edge; move the section plane slightly." (No cause or next step). step-export: main "OpenCascade could not write the named STEP assembly." → "The bodies could not be written as a STEP file. A body may hold geometry the STEP writer cannot store; rebuild the part and export again, or export STL instead." (No cause or next step). step-read: main "OpenCascade could not read this STEP file." → "This STEP file could not be read. It may be damaged or not a STEP file; export it again from the program that made it." (No cause or next step). stl-read: main "OpenCascade could not read this STL file." → "This STL file could not be read. It may be damaged or not an STL file; export it again from the program that made it." (No cause or next step). invalid-mesh (four): main "The kernel returned an invalid preview buffer size. / … invalid preview buffer pointer. / … invalid preview buffer. / … mismatched preview vertices and normals." → "The body could not be drawn: its display mesh came back incomplete. Rebuild the part. Main's sentence moves to kernelMessage." (Internal wording, no next step). topology-mapping (display, three): main "Preview translation could not identify an exact source element. / Preview translation does not preserve exact topology identity. / Preview translation changed the exact topology inventory." → "The body could not be drawn: its display faces and edges differ from the exact body. Rebuild the part; if this repeats, revise the dimensions of this feature slightly. Main's sentence moves to kernelMessage." (Internal wording, no next step). topology-mapping (pick): main "The kernel preview contains topology absent from the exact body." → "The drawn body has faces or edges the exact body does not. Rebuild the part and select again. Main's sentence moves to kernelMessage." (Internal wording, no next step). missing-body (topology reads, four): main "The topology body is unavailable. / The selected topology body is unavailable." → "This body has no faces or edges in the current build. Rebuild the part and select again." (No cause or next step). Sketch DXF export refusals, same code (Send to CAM keeps main's text): missing-sketch: main "Choose an existing sketch for CAM." → "Choose an existing sketch for DXF export." (A DXF export's refusal named CAM, which the export does not involve). suppressed-sketch: main "A suppressed sketch cannot be transferred to CAM." → "Unsuppress the sketch before exporting it as DXF." publicNotes.summary: CAD problems say what they are about, what caused them and how to repair them.
changes: The CAD header shows the problems of the current build. Each names its feature, input or body and its cause, and offers a repair where an existing action does the job: Edit feature, Choose edges again or Choose opening again.
A feature that could not be evaluated because an earlier one failed is marked as blocked in the history, and its tooltip names the cause.
In a sketch, a redundant or conflicting relation the solver names can be deleted from the issue list.
Kernel failure messages now say which step failed, the likely cause, or that the kernel named none, and what to change; the kernel's own words are under Kernel message.

When the CAD kernel or the sketch solver cannot start, stops or cannot be loaded, the message says so and what to do, and the next request tries again; the browser's own words are under Kernel message. A failing sketch solver no longer drops a drawing's inferred relations.
A refused DXF export names its code in the Export DXF dialog, and a sketch DXF export no longer says it is for CAM.
Agent replies list the problems of a build and name the feature, input, operation or export a refused edit, CAM step or DXF export concerns.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged.
